samuel2.23.p1.b1.text: These are the last words of David …

samuel2.23.p1.b2.text: … The oracle of David son of Jesse, the oracle of the man raised on high, the one anointed by the God of Jacob, and the sweet psalmist of Israel:

samuel2.23.p1.b3.text: The Spirit of the LORD spoke through me; His word was on my tongue.

samuel2.23.p2.b1.text: The God of Israel spoke; the Rock of Israel said to me,

samuel2.23.p2.b2.text: He who rules the people with justice, who rules in the fear of God,

samuel2.23.p2.b3.text: is like the light of the morning at sunrise of a cloudless dawn,

samuel2.23.p2.b4.text: the glistening after the rain on the sprouting grass of the earth.

samuel2.23.p3.b1.text: Is not my house right with God?

samuel2.23.p3.b2.text: For He has established with me an everlasting covenant, ordered and secured in every part. Will He not bring about my full salvation …

samuel2.23.p3.b3.text: But the worthless are all like thorns raked aside, … The fire burns them to ashes in the place where they lie.

samuel2.23.p4.b1.text: These are the names of David’s mighty men: Josheb-basshebeth the Tahchemonite … He wielded his spear against eight hundred men, whom he killed at one time.

samuel2.23.p4.b2.text: … struck the Philistines until his hand grew weary and stuck to his sword.

samuel2.23.p4.b3.text: When the Philistines had banded together near a field full of lentils, Israel’s troops fled from them.

samuel2.23.p4.b4.text: But Shammah took his stand in the middle of the field, defended it, and struck down the Philistines. So the LORD brought about a great victory.

samuel2.23.p5.b1.text: At harvest time, three of the thirty chief men went down to David at the cave of Adullam, … and the garrison of the Philistines was at Bethlehem.

samuel2.23.p5.b2.text: Oh, that someone would get me a drink of water from the well near the gate of Bethlehem!

samuel2.23.p5.b3.text: But he refused to drink it; instead, he poured it out to the LORD,

samuel2.23.p5.b4.text: Far be it from me, O LORD, to do this! Is this not the blood of the men who risked their lives?

samuel2.23.p6.b1.text: Now Abishai, the brother of Joab and son of Zeruiah, was chief of the Three, and he lifted his spear against three hundred men, killed them, and won a name along with the Three.

samuel2.23.p6.b2.text: And Benaiah son of Jehoiada was a man of valor from Kabzeel, a man of many exploits. He struck down two champions of Moab,

samuel2.23.p6.b3.text: and on a snowy day he went down into a pit and killed a lion.

samuel2.23.p6.b4.text: … Benaiah went against him with a club, snatched the spear from his hand, and killed the Egyptian with his own spear.

samuel2.23.p7.b1.text: Now these were members of the Thirty: Asahel the brother of Joab, Elhanan son of Dodo of Bethlehem,

samuel2.23.p7.b2.text: and Uriah the Hittite. There were thirty-seven in all.
